question: What the MONARCHTITLE message variable holds: the helper CCountry::BuildMessageVariables calls for it, and the CGovernment slot that builds the title.

addresses.name: CCountry_GetRulerTitle
addresses.comment: The whole function, 0x4FFCE0 to the bare `ret` at 0x4FFD02, then 13 int3: loads the country's `Government` (CCountry +0xDFC, never null as made) and calls its **vftable slot 15** (`[vft+0x3C]`, CGovernment::GetRulerTitle) with `out` = ESI and both flags 0 - not female, not vassal - and answers `out` in EAX. So it is the localised text of `<government key>_ruler` and nothing else: the base game's `national_socialism_ruler` is 'Führer'. **16 direct callers**, among them CCountry::BuildMessageVariables at 0x4D77AC, right after it pushes the name 'MONARCHTITLE' (0x4D7786) - which is where every message's `$MONARCHTITLE$` comes from - and CNapAction::Apply at 0xA2B23B and CEmbargoAction::Apply's message arm. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read whole in the disassembly: `mov ecx,[eax+0xdfc]; mov edx,[ecx]; mov eax,[edx+0x3c]; push 0; push 0; push esi; call eax; mov eax,esi; ret`. Slot 15 of CGovernment's vftable (0x15C25CC) and of CNullGovernment's (0x15C261C) is 0x5243F0, read off the table. Callers by a scan of .text for E8 rel32 to 0x4FFCE0 (an indirect call would be missed); 'MONARCHTITLE' read at 0x4D7786.

addresses.name: CGovernment::GetRulerTitle
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CGovernment::GetRulerTitle(CGovernment* this, Hoi3CString* out, bool female, bool vassal) @EAX
addresses.comment: **CGovernment vftable slot 15**, introduced by CGovernment and inherited unchanged by CNullGovernment. Ends `ret 0xc` at 0x524653. Builds `key = <name (+0x44)> + '_ruler'` (std::string::operatorPlus at 0x524468), appends `'_female'` when `female` (0x5244AA), then asks CGovernment::GetVassalText (0x523F70) with that key and `vassal`: where that answers something other than the key - a localised `<key>_vassal` - that is the title; otherwise it is `GetText(key)` rendered with the game settings' colours (0xA82490, then CInternationalizedText::Render at 0x5245CE). So the title is, in order: the localised `<gov>_ruler[_female]_vassal` when `vassal` is asked and that key has a text, else the localised `<gov>_ruler[_female]`. CCountry_GetRulerTitle asks it with both flags off. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read whole in the disassembly: '_ruler' pushed at 0x52441F, '_female' at 0x5244B1 behind `cmp [ebp+0xc], bl; je`, the by-value key and [ebp+0x10] passed to 0x523F70 at 0x524531, String_Equals at 0x524543 choosing between its answer (copied to out) and GetText/Render. Slot index read off the vftable at 0x15C25CC (slot 15 = 0x5243F0).

addresses.name: CGovernment::GetVassalText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CGovernment::GetVassalText(CGovernment* this, Hoi3CString* out, Hoi3CString key, bool vassal) @EAX
addresses.comment: Ends `ret 0x24` at 0x5241A7 - `out`, a by-value 0x1C-byte string and a bool. **Without `vassal`, `out` is `key` unchanged.** With it: `key + '_vassal'` (0x523FA6), asked of itself with `vassal` off (so the same text back), looked up with GetText and rendered (0x52404E, 0x524059); where the rendered text equals the `_vassal` key - no localisation has it - `out` is the original `key`, else the rendered text. Three direct callers, all in CGovernment: itself (0x524040), CGovernment slot 13 (0x5242CF) and slot 15, CGovernment::GetRulerTitle (0x524531) - which tells the two apart by comparing the answer with the key. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read whole in the disassembly: the `cmp [ebp+0x28], bl; je 0x524162` test at 0x523F9B, the plain-copy exit at 0x524162-0x52417F, String_Equals at 0x5240C5 choosing between the rendered text and `key`. Callers by an E8 rel32 scan of .text.
